Provenance.drafts: An A/B control ran first at seed 700100 (denoise 0.8) with IPAdapter OFF vs ON, 4 candidates each, to prove the adapter moves palette and not shape -- both sides missed structurally (a round hut, splitting into two huts, a giant pot eating the building) and were abandoned regardless of adapter state; this is the in-repo evidence sheet 'evidence - IPA on vs off, same seed - style moves to anchor, shape does not.png'. Seed 700600 (denoise 0.7, IPAdapter on, 4 candidates) against the U3 Building clause: #1 read as a house, not a tavern; #2's roof seam visually split the building's mass in two; #4 was clean but plain with a hanging sign. #3 (two-story inn massing, a sign band over the door, sitting naturally beside the Shop) was the clear winner.
Provenance.paintoverNote: #3 taken as-is, no inpaint needed -- the two-story silhouette, warm-lit windows and sign band already matched the Building clause and read well next to market.png's own massing.
Provenance.aiDisclosure: AI-generated (SDXL base 1.0 + pixel-art-xl LoRA) diffuse, single ComfyUI KSampler pass (seed 700600, denoise 0.7) -- read directly from the PNG's own embedded ComfyUI workflow JSON, not quoted from memory. IPAdapterAdvanced (vit-h, style transfer, weight 0.9) referenced market.png so palette and lighting lock to the shipped Shop. DEVIATION from cutout.py: background removed via a deterministic flood-fill alpha matte (border-color median, border-seeded flood-fill of the core-background mask, then a fixed ~5px feather ring), not the BiRefNet model cutout.py wraps -- this render's backdrop measured near-uniform (border std < 1.3 per channel) so a segmentation-model pass bought nothing; cutout.py/BiRefNet remains the tool of record for gradient or busy backgrounds. Cropped to the alpha content box, then BOX-downsampled straight to 84x88 (no hard quantization) -- the same recipe market.png's own committed pixels were produced by. Replaces the prior unreproducible-legacy asset, which KTD-A's contract measured as baked green hedges/a purple road/a cream path spilling past the building's own footprint on three sides.
